2.response: Proposed questions for MCC: (1) provide the Appendix B application and technology inventory referenced by PWS 2.2 and 4.2.1.1, with dependencies, data classifications, support tiers, usage and available incident/change history; (2) reconcile RFI 5.c's reference to Section 5.0 deliverables with the issued PWS's Section 5.0 Labor Requirements, identify the applicable deliverable/acceptance schedule and Section H key-personnel designations, and reconcile the Scope paragraph's Section 4.4 Infrastructure reference with the issued Section 4.4 Application Administration; (3) identify each application's development, test, staging and production owner, approval path and access lead times; (4) provide the current pipeline tools, infrastructure interfaces, patch windows, restore objectives and operational acceptance criteria; (5) define service hours, on-call expectations and severity-based targets in addition to the stated Eastern core hours; (6) specify the backlog, expected enhancement volume and boundary between recurring O&M and separately ordered surge work; and (7) clarify modernization budget, platform/license constraints, data migration responsibilities and acceptance authority. The acquired October 6 resource index contains the RFI, PWS and Industry Day notice; the referenced Appendix B and Section H are not included in that three-file packet.
2.reviewNote: Proposed market-research feedback for company selection. The original SAM RFI/PWS files confirm the existing questions and cross-reference issues. Appendix B and Section H remain requests for the actual referenced material. Actual issuer answers should be retained as question_response sources.

5.c.response: For each ordered new application or significant change, agree a tailored deliverable and acceptance checklist using PWS 4.3.1. The stated documentation set covers system design; test plans, cases, files/data and problem support; development, data migration, integration and implementation plans; operations, administration and training guidance; certification/accreditation and authorization artifacts where applicable; system documentation; configuration requests; version control; lessons learned; bug/enhancement records; legacy-system disposition; and staffing plans. Bind each required item to the delivered source/configuration, selected environment, responsible author and Government acceptance decision. Deliver changed documentation with major and minor releases in the specified electronic formats, including MCC's stated Word/Excel conventions, and write user guidance for a new nontechnical user. Reuse the authoritative delivery records to provide the exact tailored set. For an FFP increment, identify the accepted outcome, interfaces, data migrations, recovery procedure, included documentation and open exceptions in one receiving package.
5.c.reviewNote: RFI 5.c still names Section 5.0; issued PWS 5.0 is Labor Requirements. The actual new-development documentation provisions are in PWS 4.3.1, body elements 287–306. Government task tailoring selects the required set; the RFI cross-reference remains an explicit clarification item.

5.d.response: Start the staffing design with the functions the issued PWS expressly names: a Program Manager responsible for the entirety of contract delivery and performance, and Enterprise and AI Architects or other appropriate labor categories for solutions-architecture support. Map the further functions to the application inventory and workload: product/business analysis, application and platform engineering, service/DevSecOps coordination, security, data engineering, accessibility and specialist platform support. A qualified person may cover compatible functions where capacity and independence permit. Identify each responsibility, delivery output, backup and escalation path before sizing positions. Plan for the PWS's Washington, D.C. Metro expectation for key personnel and Eastern core operating hours. Obtain Section H's actual key-personnel designations and the responding company's qualified, available nominees before presenting a named staffing commitment.
5.d.reviewNote: Issued PWS 4.1.1 names the Program Manager; 4.1.4 names Enterprise and AI Architects or appropriate labor categories; 3.0 gives location/core-hours context; 5.1 points to Section H. These provisions support the staffing design while company qualifications and availability retain their existing review status.

7.a.response: Maintain a workload-based staffing plan by application/service and delivery function. Use the actual inventory, incoming support demand, backlog, release calendar, service objectives and specialist dependencies to size a stable operating team and identify separately planned changes or surge work. Review demand and capacity with MCC, make the effect of each staffing change visible, and retain knowledge-transfer and backup coverage when people rotate. Match the operating model to the issued PWS: primary work at contractor or telework sites, key personnel expected in the Washington, D.C. Metro area, and generally 09:00–15:00 Eastern core hours with customer operating-hours and meeting/response obligations. Separate approved after-hours coverage from dedicated staffing. Prepare a phase-in plan within the PWS's maximum 60-calendar-day transition and coordinate with the incumbent so service and active work remain continuous. Confirm actual personnel, skills and availability through the responding company's staffing and partner records.
7.a.reviewNote: Original PWS 3.0, 4.1.1 and 4.1.2.1 supply operating and transition constraints; its workload-flexibility provisions remain the basis for right-sizing. The 60-day phase-in maximum is distinct from the 14-day written surge-proposal requirement.

7.c.response: Build a surge readiness matrix by specialty with the actual candidate or partner pool, relevant experience, availability, employment/contracting route, access and investigation dependencies, onboarding steps and release from other work. For each written MCC surge request, prepare the scope, schedules, deliverables, labor, other direct costs and budget proposal within fourteen calendar days as PWS 4.3.2 requires, and obtain MCC's approval of tasking and schedule before surge work begins. State separate anticipated dates for request triage, candidate identification, skills review, contracting, Government approvals, investigation/access, onboarding and productive deployment. Support each offered staffing timeline with the actual person or partner's availability and the applicable access assumptions; include an exit and knowledge-transfer step when the temporary demand ends.
7.c.reviewNote: RFI 7.c invites actual anticipated deployment timing. PWS 4.3.2 sets a 14-calendar-day proposal requirement, while PWS 5.2/5.3 supplies investigation and identity-verification dependencies. The existing team_required/unanswered decision remains until the company supplies its reviewed capacity and timeline.

11.a.response: Use an application/service inventory with accountable owners, dependency and environment maps, support tier, business criticality, usage, change demand and observed incidents to size O&M coverage. Align the operating workflow to MCC's issued responsibilities: the separate Service Desk vendor provides Tier 1 and most Tier 2; Digital Services provides some Tier 2 and Tier 3, records work in the approved ticketing system, and coordinates with operations/security vendors. Production changes pass through MCC change control and are executed by the responsible vendor or OCIO CI/CD pipeline, with the stated SharePoint, ServiceNow and Box.com elevated-permission exceptions mapped explicitly. Provide diagnosis, workarounds, fixes, patch-impact validation, compatibility checks, application monitoring and knowledge transfer to lower support tiers. Reassess capacity as products move from development through maintenance to retirement; separate database/application expertise from the other vendor's general infrastructure administration. Keep emergency continuity work within the agreed staffing model and prepare recovery and handover procedures for actual selected applications.
11.a.reviewNote: Primary PWS 4.2.1/4.2.2 and 4.4 supply the support, production and administration boundaries. Application-specific sizing still depends on the referenced inventory and actual demand. The workflow preserves the existing vendor/customer change authority.

14.a.response: Begin with the actual application and data inventory, dependencies, usage, support burden, security requirements and running costs. Group applications by migration suitability, then agree a target pattern using managed platform, data and identity services where they meet the workload and MCC's standards. Establish repeatable infrastructure/application configuration, an automated build and promotion path, explicit environment and production responsibilities, operational monitoring, backup/restore and an exercised rollback before migrating a selected application. Move incrementally by application or dependency group and compare the accepted result against the original service and cost baseline. Assess data conversion, compatibility, licensing, portability, availability and operating skills alongside expected savings. Follow the PWS's requirement to propose middleware and obtain Government agreement on security and future maintenance/support costs; retain the selected platform and recurring-cost decisions. Coordinate database/application expertise with the existing infrastructure provider and OCIO pipeline owners.
14.a.reviewNote: The issued PWS identifies a largely cloud-based Microsoft/AWS/O365 environment, current SQL Server/MySQL standards, application/database work and separate infrastructure responsibilities. This remains a proposed modernization approach; final target selection follows the actual Appendix B inventory and company review.
